l: Island of Onogoro, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Island of Onogoro forms when brine dripping from the heavenly jewelled spear is piled up after the brine has been stirred until it goes curdle-curdle.

l: command to make, consolidate, and give birth to the drifting land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Heavenly Deities give this command to the Male-Who-Invites and Female-Who-Invites. The command leads them to stir the brine with the heavenly jewelled spear and produce the Island of Onogoro.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Courtship of the Deities the Male-Who-Invites and the Female Who-Invites begins after they descend from Heaven onto the island and erect an heavenly august pillar and an hall of eight fathoms. Augustus Mas-Qui-Invitat and Augusta Femina-Qui-Invitat discuss their bodies and agree that his superfluous part should be inserted into her undeveloped part to procreate regions. They circle the heavenly august pillar and unite, but Augusta Femina-Qui-Invitat speaks first, which Augustus Mas-Qui-Invitat says is improper for a woman. They produce Hirudinem, whom they place in a reed boat and let float away, and then produce the Island of Aha, which is not counted among their children.

l: Courtship of the Deities the Male-Who-Invites and the Female Who-Invites, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Courtship concerns Augustus Mas-Qui-Invitat and Augusta Femina-Qui-Invitat after they descend from Heaven onto the island. They erect an heavenly august pillar and an hall of eight fathoms, agree to unite for procreation, and produce Hirudinem and the Island of Aha.

l: Augustus Mas-Qui-Invitat, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Augustus Mas-Qui-Invitat asks Augusta Femina-Qui-Invitat about her body and proposes inserting his superfluous part into her undeveloped part to procreate regions. He directs their circling of the heavenly august pillar, reproves Augusta Femina-Qui-Invitat for speaking first, and helps produce Hirudinem and the Island of Aha.

l: Augusta Femina-Qui-Invitat, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Augusta Femina-Qui-Invitat says that her body has one part that did not grow continuously and agrees that Augustus Mas-Qui-Invitat may insert his superfluous part into it. She speaks first after circling the heavenly august pillar, then unites with Augustus Mas-Qui-Invitat and gives birth to Hirudinem and the Island of Aha.

l: island, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The island is where Augustus Mas-Qui-Invitat and Augusta Femina-Qui-Invitat descend from Heaven. On it, they erect an heavenly august pillar and an hall of eight fathoms.

l: Hirudinem, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Hirudinem is the first child produced by Augustus Mas-Qui-Invitat and Augusta Femina-Qui-Invitat. They place Hirudinem in a boat of reeds and let it float away.

l: Island of Aha, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Island of Aha is produced after Hirudinem by Augustus Mas-Qui-Invitat and Augusta Femina-Qui-Invitat. It is not reckoned among their children.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The two Deities learn that their first children were not good because the woman spoke first, so they consult the Heavenly Deities and repeat the ritual with the Male-Who-Invites speaking first. They then give birth to the eight islands known as the Land-of-the-Eight-Great-Islands, including the Island of Ahaji, Ho-no-sa-wake, the Island of Futa-no, the Islands of Mitsu-go, the Island of Iki, the Island of Tsu, the Island of Sado, and Great-Yamato-the-Luxuriant-Island-of-the-Dragon-Fly. Afterward, they give birth to six additional islands.

l: the two Deities, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The two Deities determine that their first children were not good, consult the Heavenly Deities, and are instructed to descend and amend their words. They repeat the ritual, with the Male-Who-Invites speaking first, and give birth to the eight islands and then six additional islands.

l: His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Male-Who-Invites speaks first after the two Deities repeat the ritual, saying, "Ah! what a fair and lovely maiden!"

l: Her Augustness the Princess-Who-Invites, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Female-Who-Invites speaks after the Male-Who-Invites, saying, "Ah! what a fair and lovely youth!"

l: the birth of the Eight Islands, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: After the Male-Who-Invites speaks first, the two Deities give birth to eight islands. These islands give rise to the name Land-of-the-Eight-Great-Islands because they were born first.

l: the Island of Ahaji, Ho-no-sa-wake, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The two Deities give birth to the Island of Ahaji, Ho-no-sa-wake, after repeating their ritual.

l: the Island of Futa-no, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The two Deities give birth to the Island of Futa-no in Iyo. It has one body and four faces, named the Land of Iyo, the Land of Sanuki, the Land of Aha, and the Land of Tosa.

l: the Islands of Mitsu-go, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The two Deities give birth to the Islands of Mitsu-go near Oki, also called Heavenly-Great-Heart-Youth. The islands have one body and four faces, each with a separate name.

l: the Island of Iki, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The two Deities give birth to the Island of Iki, also called Heaven's One-Pillar.

l: the Island of Tsu, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The two Deities give birth to the Island of Tsu, also called Heavenly-Hand-net-Good-Princess.

l: the Island of Sado, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The two Deities give birth to the Island of Sado.

l: Great-Yamato-the-Luxuriant-Island-of-the-Dragon-Fly, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The two Deities give birth to Great-Yamato-the-Luxuriant-Island-of-the-Dragon-Fly, also called Heavenly-August-Sky-Luxuriant-Dragon-fly-Lord-Youth. It is the eighth island born among the Land-of-the-Eight-Great-Islands.

l: Land-of-the-Eight-Great-Islands, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The name Land-of-the-Eight-Great-Islands originates from the eight islands that were born first: the Island of Ahaji, Ho-no-sa-wake, the Island of Futa-no, the Islands of Mitsu-go, the Island of Iki, the Island of Tsu, the Island of Sado, and Great-Yamato-the-Luxuriant-Island-of-the-Dragon-Fly.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: This unit concerns the birth of various deities after the birth of countries. Great-Male-of-the-Great-Thing is the first deity named in a sequence of ten deities, followed by deities associated with water, wind, trees, mountains, moors, valleys, food, and fire. Prince-of-Swift-Autumn and Princess-of-Swift-Autumn give birth from their separate dominions of river and sea to eight water-related deities.

l: Great-Male-of-the-Great-Thing, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Great-Male-of-the-Great-Thing is the first deity born in the renewed sequence of births after the countries. He is included among the ten deities born from Great-Male-of-the-Great-Thing to Princess-of-Autumn.

l: Prince-of-Swift-Autumn, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Prince-of-Swift-Autumn is the Deity of the Water-Gates and is born after the Deity Great-House-Prince and other deities. Together with his younger sister Princess-of-Swift-Autumn, he gives birth from his separate dominion of river to eight water-related deities.

l: Princess-of-Swift-Autumn, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Princess-of-Swift-Autumn is the younger sister of Prince-of-Swift-Autumn and is born as the Deity of the Water-Gates. Together with Prince-of-Swift-Autumn, she gives birth from her separate dominion of sea to eight water-related deities.

l: birth of the various deities, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: After the birth of countries, the deities begin giving birth to various deities. The births include deities associated with water, wind, trees, mountains, moors, passes, valleys, food, and fire.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Her Augustness the Princess-Who-Invites sickened after giving birth to the Deity-of-Fire because her august private parts were burnt, and she divinely retired. Deities were born from her vomit, faeces, and urine, including the Deity Metal-Mountain-Prince, the Deity Clay-Viscid-Prince, the Deity Mitsuhanome, and the Young-Wondrous-Producing-Deity. His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites mourned her and said that he had exchanged her for their single child. He buried her on Mount Hiba at the boundary of the Land of Idzumo and the Land of Hahaki, while his tears gave birth to the Crying-Weeping-Female-Deity.

l: Her Augustness the Princess-Who-Invites, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Through giving birth to the Deity-of-Fire, her august private parts were burnt, and she sickened and lay down. She divinely retired, and His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites buried her on Mount Hiba.

l: His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites lamented that he had exchanged Her Augustness the Princess-Who-Invites for their single child. As he wept while creeping round her august pillow and feet, his tears gave birth to the Crying-Weeping-Female-Deity.

l: Deity-of-Fire, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Deity-of-Fire was born to Her Augustness the Princess-Who-Invites. Through giving birth to the Deity-of-Fire, she was burned and ultimately divinely retired.

l: Crying-Weeping-Female-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Crying-Weeping-Female-Deity was born from the august tears of His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites. The Deity dwells at Konomoto near Unewo on Mount Kagu.

l: Mount Hiba, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Mount Hiba was the place where His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites buried the divinely retired Deity the Female-Who-Invites. It was at the boundary of the Land of Idzumo and the Land of Hahaki.

l: birth of the Deity-of-Fire, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The birth of the Deity-of-Fire burned the august private parts of Her Augustness the Princess-Who-Invites. After this birth, she sickened, lay down, and divinely retired.

l: divine retirement of the Princess-Who-Invites, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Princess-Who-Invites divinely retired after giving birth to the Deity-of-Fire and becoming sick. Her divinely retired body was buried on Mount Hiba by His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites.

l: burial of the Female-Who-Invites, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites buried the divinely retired Deity the Female-Who-Invites on Mount Hiba. The burial place was at the boundary of the Land of Idzumo and the Land of Hahaki.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: His Augustness the Male-Who-invites cuts off the head of his child, the Deity Shining-Elder, with a ten-grasp sabre. Blood from the august sword gives birth to eight Deities, while the slain Deity Shining-Elder gives birth to eight Deities from different parts of his body. The sword is named Heavenly-Point-Blade-Extended and Majestic Point-Blade-Extended.

l: The Slaying of the Fire-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The unit concerns the slaying of the Deity Shining-Elder by His Augustness the Male-Who-invites and the Deities born from the sword and from the slain body.

l: His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: His Augustness the Male-Who-invites draws the ten-grasp sabre girded on him and cuts off the head of his child, the Deity Shining-Elder.

l: the Deity Shining-Elder, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Deity Shining-Elder is slain when His Augustness the Male-Who-invites cuts off his head. Eight Deities are then born from his head, chest, belly, private parts, hands, and feet.

l: Heavenly-Point-Blade-Extended, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Heavenly-Point-Blade-Extended is one name of the sword with which His Augustness the Male-Who-invites cuts off the head of the Deity Shining-Elder.

l: Majestic Point-Blade-Extended, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Majestic Point-Blade-Extended is another name for the sword with which His Augustness the Male-Who-invites cuts off the head of the Deity Shining-Elder.

l: ten-grasp sabre, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Blood from the point, upper part, and hilt of the august sword gives birth to eight Deities. The sword is named Heavenly-Point-Blade-Extended and Majestic Point-Blade-Extended.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites follows Her Augustness the Female-Who-Invites to the Land of Hades and asks her to return because the lands made by the siblings are unfinished. He sees her rotting body and the eight Thunder-Deities dwelling in it, then flees while she sends pursuers after him. Three peaches help him repel the pursuers, and he blocks the Even Pass of Hades with a thousand-draught rock. Her Augustness the Female-Who-Invites and His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites exchange threats concerning death and birth, after which she is called the Great-Deity-of-Hades and the Even Pass of Hades is called the Ifuya-Pass.

l: His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites follows Her Augustness the Female-Who-Invites to the Land of Hades and asks her to return because the lands made by the siblings are unfinished. He looks at her rotting body, flees from her, uses his head-dress and comb to create food that delays his pursuers, and uses three peaches to repel them. He blocks the Even Pass of Hades with a thousand-draught rock and declares that a thousand and five hundred parturition-houses will be established each day if she kills a thousand people daily.

l: Her Augustness the Princess-Who-Invites, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Her Augustness the Female-Who-Invites says that she has eaten of the furnace of Hades and agrees to discuss returning with the Deities of Hades. After His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites looks at her, she sends the Ugly-Female-of-Hades, the eight Thunder-Deities, and warriors to pursue him, and later pursues him herself. She threatens to strangle a thousand people of his land each day and is thereafter called the Great-Deity-of-Hades.

l: Land of Hades, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Land of Hades is where Her Augustness the Female-Who-Invites resides after eating of its furnace. It contains her palace, the Deities of Hades, the Ugly-Female-of-Hades, the eight Thunder-Deities, and warriors who pursue His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites.

l: lands made by the siblings, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The lands made by His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites and Her Augustness the Female-Who-Invites are not yet finished making.

l: Even Pass of Hades, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Even Pass of Hades is where His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites reaches the base and repels his pursuers with three peaches. He blocks it with a thousand-draught rock, and it is later called the Ifuya-Pass in the Land of Idzumo.

l: three peaches, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The three peaches grow at the base of the Even Pass of Hades. His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites uses them to smite the pursuers, and he gives them the designation of Their Augustnesses Great-Divine-Fruit after they help him.

l: thousand-draught rock, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The thousand-draught rock is drawn by His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites and used to block the Even Pass of Hades. It is placed between him and Her Augustness the Female-Who-Invites as they exchange leave-takings.

l: Great-Deity-of-Hades, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Her Augustness the Female-Who-Invites is called the Great-Deity-of-Hades after she pursues and reaches His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites.

l: Ifuya-Pass, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Ifuya-Pass is the later name for the Even Pass of Hades in the Land of Idzumo.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The unit concerns the purification of the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites after he reaches a hideous and polluted land. At a small river-mouth near Tachibana in Himuka, he removes his clothing and accessories, from which twelve Deities are born, then bathes in the middle reach of the water. His bathing produces Deities of evils, rectification, the ocean depths and surfaces, and finally the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity, His Augustness, Moon-Night Possessor, and His Brave-Swift-impetuous-Male-Augustness. The three Ocean-Possessing Deities are ancestral Deities of the Chiefs of Adzumi, while three others are the three Great Deities of the Inlet of Sumi.

l: The Purification of the August Person, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: It concerns the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites cleansing himself after coming to a hideous and polluted land. The purification includes removing the things on his person and bathing in different parts of the water.

l: His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: He declares that he has come to a hideous and polluted land and decides to purify his august person. He removes his clothing and accessories, then bathes in the middle reach of a small river, producing numerous Deities.

l: a small river-mouth near Tachibana in Himuka, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites goes to a plain covered with ahagi at this small river-mouth and purifies and cleanses himself there.

l: the Deity Possessor-of-the-Ocean-Bottom, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: He is born as the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites bathes at the bottom of the water.

l: His Augustness Elder-Male-of-the-Bottom, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: He is born as the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites bathes at the bottom of the water. He is one of the three Great Deities of the Inlet of Sumi.

l: the Deity Possessor-of-the-Ocean-Middle, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: He is born as the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites bathes in the middle of the water.

l: His Augustness Elder-Male-of-the-Middle, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: He is born as the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites bathes in the middle of the water. He is one of the three Great Deities of the Inlet of Sumi.

l: the Deity Possessor-of-the-Ocean-Surface, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: He is born as the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites bathes at the top of the water.

l: His Augustness Elder-Male-of-the-Surface, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: He is born as the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites bathes at the top of the water. He is one of the three Great Deities of the Inlet of Sumi.

l: the three Ocean-Possessing Deities, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: They are the Deity Possessor-of-the-Ocean-Bottom, the Deity Possessor-of-the-Ocean-Middle, and the Deity Possessor-of-the-Ocean-Surface. They are revered as ancestral Deities by the Chiefs of Adzumi.

l: the Chiefs of Adzumi, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: They hold the three Ocean-Possessing Deities in reverence as their ancestral Deities. They are descendants of His Augustness Utsushi-hi-gana-saku, a child of these Ocean-Possessing Deities.

l: the three Great Deities of the Inlet of Sumi, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: They are His Augustness Elder-Male-of-the-Bottom, His Augustness Elder-Male-of-the-Middle, and His Augustness Elder-Male-of-the-Surface.

l: Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: She is born when the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites washes his left august eye.

l: His Augustness, Moon-Night Possessor, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: He is born when the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites washes his right august eye.

l: His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: He is born when the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites washes his august nose.

l: the purification of the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: It takes place at a small river-mouth near Tachibana in Himuka after the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites reaches a hideous and polluted land. It produces Deities through the removal of his garments and accessories and through bathing in the water.

l: the bathing of the Great Deity the Male-Who-Invites, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: He first plunges into the middle reach because the upper reach is too rapid and the lower reach too sluggish. As he bathes at the bottom, middle, and surface of the water and washes his eyes and nose, multiple Deities are born.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites rejoices after begetting three illustrious children and invests them with rule. He gives the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity authority over the Plain-of-High-Heaven, Moon-Night-Possessor authority over the Dominion of the Night, and His-Brave-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness authority over the Sea-Plain. His-Brave-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness instead cries and weeps because he wishes to depart to the Nether Distant Land. His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites becomes angry and drives him out by a divine expulsion.

l: Investiture of the Three Deities, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites invests the three illustrious children with authority over different domains.

l: the Three Deities, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Three Deities are the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity, Moon-Night-Possessor, and His-Brave-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness. The first two assume their assigned rule, while the third does not.

l: His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites rejoices at begetting three illustrious children and assigns each one a domain to rule. He becomes angry with His-Brave-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness and expels him.

l: Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity receives the August necklace and is charged to rule the Plain-of-High-Heaven.

l: Moon-Night-Possessor, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Moon-Night-Possessor is charged to rule the Dominion of the Night.

l: His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: His-Brave-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness is charged to rule the Sea-Plain but does not assume that rule. He cries and weeps because he wishes to depart to the Nether Distant Land, and His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites expels him.

l: Plain-of-High-Heaven, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Plain-of-High-Heaven is assigned to the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity to rule.

l: Sea-Plain, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Sea-Plain is assigned to His-Brave-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness to rule, but he does not take up the charge.

l: Crying and Weeping of His Impetuous-Male-Augustness, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness cries and weeps so intensely that his eight-grasp beard reaches his stomach. His weeping withers the green mountains, dries the rivers and seas, and brings forth portents of woe.

l: Nether Distant Land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Nether Distant Land is the deceased mother's land to which His-Brave-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness wishes to depart.

l: The August Expulsion of His-Impetuous-Male-Augustness, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The divine expulsion removes His-Brave-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness from the land after His Augustness the Male-Who-Invites rejects his wish to depart.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness ascends to Heaven after being expelled, intending to take leave of the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity. The Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity prepares for a possible attack and questions his intentions. They establish the August Oath by swearing and producing children from a sabre and curved jewels. Several deities are born from the mist of their breath, with five attributed to each act of producing children.

l: His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: He ascends to Heaven after being divinely expelled, saying that he wishes only to take leave of the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity and depart. He swears with her and produces several deities from the curved jewels taken from her hair, head-dress, and arms.

l: Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: She fears that His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness intends to seize her land, so she arms herself and challenges him. After hearing his explanation, she agrees to test his sincerity by swearing and producing children.

l: Heaven, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness goes up to Heaven, causing the mountains, rivers, lands, and countries to shake and quake.

l: The August Oath, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The August Oath is established when the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity and His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness swear to each other and produce children from a sabre and curved jewels.

l: swearing and producing children, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Swearing and producing children serves as the test of sincerity between the two deities. Their actions produce deities from mist formed when the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity and His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness crunch and blow away the sabre fragments and jewels.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity declares that the five male Deities born last are her children, while the three female Deities born first are His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness's children. The three female Deities dwell in the inner, middle, and outer temples of Munakata and are revered by the Dukes of Munakata. His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness then claims victory, ravages the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity's ricefields and palace, and releases a flayed heavenly piebald horse into her weaving-hall. The women weaving the heavenly garments are alarmed, injure their private parts against the shuttle's rays, and die.

l: The August Declaration of the Division of the August Male Children and the August Female Children, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: This declaration assigns the five male Deities born last to Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity and the three female Deities born first to His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness. It also states where the three female Deities dwell and identifies their reverence by the Dukes of Munakata.

l: The August Ravages of His Impetuous-Male-Augustness, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: This section concerns the ravages committed by His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness against Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity. He breaks down ricefield divisions, fills up ditches, strews excrements in the palace, and releases a flayed heavenly piebald horse into the weaving-hall.

l: Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity declares the division of the children, assigning the five male Deities born last to herself and the three female Deities born first to His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness. She excuses His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness's ravages before he continues them, and she is present in the weaving-hall when the flayed heavenly piebald horse is released.

l: His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness is declared the parent of the three female Deities born first. Claiming victory, he ravages Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity's ricefields and palace and releases a flayed heavenly piebald horse into her weaving-hall.

l: five deities born from the mist, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The five male Deities born last are declared to be the children of Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity because their birth was from things of hers.

l: the three female Deities born first, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The three female Deities born first are declared to be the children of His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness because their birth was from a thing of his. They dwell in the three temples of Munakata.

l: Her Augustness Torrent-Mist-Princess, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Her Augustness Torrent-Mist-Princess is the first of the three female Deities born first and dwells in the Inner temple of Munakata.

l: Her Augustness Lovely-Island-Princess, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Her Augustness Lovely-Island-Princess is the second of the three female Deities born first and dwells in the middle temple of Munakata.

l: Her Augustness Princess-of-the-Torrent, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Her Augustness Princess-of-the-Torrent is the third of the three female Deities born first and dwells in the outer temple of Munakata.

l: the three Great Deities held in reverence by the Dukes of Munakata, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The three Great Deities held in reverence by the Dukes of Munakata are Her Augustness Torrent-Mist-Princess, Her Augustness Lovely-Island-Princess, and Her Augustness Princess-of-the-Torrent.

l: His Augustness Brave-Rustic-Illuminator, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: His Augustness Brave-Rustic-Illuminator is a child of His Augustness Ame-no-hohi and one of the five children born afterwards. The text identifies him as an ancestor of several rulers and departmental suzerains.

l: His Augustness Prince-Lord-of-Heaven, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: His Augustness Prince-Lord-of-Heaven is identified as an ancestor of several rulers, chiefs, suzerains, and territorial lords.

l: Munakata, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Munakata has an Inner temple, a middle temple, and an outer temple. The three female Deities born first dwell in these temples, and the three Great Deities are held in reverence by the Dukes of Munakata.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity closes and fastens the door of the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling, causing the Plain of High Heaven and the Central Land of Reed-Plains to become dark and eternal night to prevail. The myriad Deities assemble in the bed of the Tranquil River of Heaven and devise a plan involving offerings, a mirror, curved jewels, divination, singing birds, and the actions of several Deities. The Heavenly-Alarming Female performs a ritual before the door, causing the eight hundred myriad Deities to laugh and the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity to open the door slightly. The Heavenly-Beckoning-Ancestor-Lord and Great-Jewel show her the mirror, and the Heavenly Hand-Strength-Male-Deity draws her out, restoring light to both lands.

l: Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity closes and fastens the door of the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling and retires, causing darkness and eternal night. She later opens the door slightly, comes forth after seeing the mirror, and her emergence restores light to the Plain of High Heaven and the Central Land of Reed-Plains.

l: Heavenly Rock-Dwelling, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Heavenly Rock-Dwelling is the place into which the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity retires. Its door is closed and fastened, then later opened slightly so that she can gaze upon the mirror and come forth.

l: door (Heavenly Rock-Dwelling), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The door of the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling is closed and fastened by the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity. The Heavenly-Alarming Female performs before it, and the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity later opens it slightly before being drawn out.

l: Plain of High Heaven, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Plain of High Heaven becomes obscured when the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity retires. It later shakes during the Heavenly-Alarming Female's performance and becomes light again when the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity comes forth.

l: Central Land of Reed-Plains, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Central Land of Reed-Plains becomes dark when the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity retires. It becomes light again after she is drawn out from the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling.

l: eternal night, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Eternal night prevails after the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity closes herself inside the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling. The long-singing birds of eternal night are assembled and made to sing as part of the plan to bring her out.

l: eight hundred myriad Deities, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The voices of the myriad Deities are heard like flies in the fifth moon, and myriad portents of woe arise. The eight hundred myriad Deities assemble in a divine assembly, later laugh together, and assist in the plan to bring the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity out.

l: Deity Thought-Includer, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Deity Thought-Includer is ordered to think of a plan during the assembly of the eight hundred myriad Deities.

l: mirror, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: A mirror eight feet long is made and tied to the middle branches of a true cleyera japonica. The Heavenly-Beckoning-Ancestor-Lord and Great-Jewel push it forward and show it to the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity, who gazes upon it and comes forth.

l: His Augustness Heavenly-Beckoning-Ancestor-Lord, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Heavenly-Beckoning-Ancestor-Lord is summoned to assist with the plan, helps pull out the shoulder-blade of a true stag and perform divination, and prayerfully recites grand liturgies. He later pushes the mirror forward to show it to the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity and helps draw her out by pulling the bottom-tied rope along her back.

l: Great-Jewel, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Great-Jewel is summoned to assist with the plan and takes the divers things together with the grand august Offerings. Great-Jewel later helps push the mirror forward to show it to the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity and draws the bottom-tied rope along her back.

l: Heavenly Mount Kagu, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Heavenly Mount Kagu provides the shoulder-blade of a true stag, cherrybark, a true cleyera japonica, heavenly clubmoss, a heavenly spindle-tree, and bamboo-grass for the plan and the performance before the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling.

l: Heavenly Hand-Strength-Male-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Heavenly Hand-Strength-Male-Deity stands hidden beside the door of the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling. When the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity comes forth, he takes her august hand and draws her out.

l: Heavenly-Alarming-Female, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Heavenly-Alarming Female hangs heavenly clubmoss around herself, wears a heavenly spindle-tree as a head-dress, binds bamboo-grass in a posy, and performs before the door as if possessed by a Deity. Her performance makes the Plain of High Heaven shake and causes the eight hundred myriad Deities to laugh, leading the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity to open the door slightly.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The eight hundred myriad Deities impose a fine on High-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness, cut his beard, pull out his fingernails and toenails, and expel him. Afterward, he begs food from Princess-of-Great-Food, who offers dishes made from things taken from her nose, mouth, and fundament. Believing she has offered him filth, he kills Princess-of-Great-Food. From her body come silkworms, rice-seeds, millet, small beans, barley, and large beans, which Deity-Producing-Wondrous-Ancestor causes to be used as seeds.

l: The August Expulsion of His-Impetuous-Male-Augustness, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: It concerns the expulsion of High-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness after the eight hundred myriad Deities impose a fine, cut his beard, and pull out his fingernails and toenails.

l: His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The eight hundred myriad Deities fine him a thousand tables, cut his beard, pull out his fingernails and toenails, and expel him. Afterward, he begs food from Princess-of-Great-Food and kills her because he believes she has offered him filth.

l: eight hundred myriad Deities, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: They take counsel together and punish High-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness by imposing a fine, cutting his beard, pulling out his fingernails and toenails, and expelling him.

l: Princess-of-Great-Food, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: She takes dainty things from her nose, mouth, and fundament, makes them into dishes, and offers them to High-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness. He kills her, and silkworms, rice-seeds, millet, small beans, barley, and large beans are born from her body.

l: Deity-Producing-Wondrous-Ancestor, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Deity-Producing-Wondrous-Ancestor causes the things born from the body of Princess-of-Great-Food to be taken and used as seeds.

l: seeds, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The seeds include silkworms from the head, rice-seeds from the two eyes, millet from the two ears, small beans from the nose, barley from the private parts, and large beans from the fundament of Princess-of-Great-Food.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness descends from Heaven to the head-waters of the River Hi and finds Foot-Stroking-Elder, Hand-Stroking Elder, and Wondrous-Inada-Princess mourning the annual devouring of their daughters by the eight-forked serpent of Koshi. He agrees to protect Wondrous-Inada-Princess and directs the preparation of a liquor trap using eight-fold refined liquor, eight gates, platforms, and vats. After the serpent becomes intoxicated, he cuts it into pieces with his ten-grasp sabre. A great sword is discovered inside the serpent's middle tail and is respectfully reported to the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity as the Herb-Quelling Great Sword.

l: His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: He descends from Heaven to the head-waters of the River Hi, where he meets Foot-Stroking-Elder, Hand-Stroking Elder, and Wondrous-Inada-Princess. He agrees to protect Wondrous-Inada-Princess, arranges a liquor trap, intoxicates the eight-forked serpent of Koshi, and cuts it into pieces.

l: River Hi, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The River Hi is the river at whose head-waters His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness encounters the grieving family. After the eight-forked serpent is cut apart, its waters flow changed into a river of blood.

l: old man (Foot-Stroking-Elder), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: He identifies himself as an Earthly Deity and a child of the Deity Great-Mountain-Possessor. He explains that the eight-forked serpent of Koshi has devoured seven of his eight daughters and agrees to offer Wondrous-Inada-Princess to His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness.

l: old woman (Hand-Stroking Elder), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: She is the wife of Foot-Stroking-Elder and is present with him and Wondrous-Inada-Princess while they weep over the serpent's expected arrival.

l: Wondrous-Inada-Princess, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: She is the daughter of Foot-Stroking-Elder and Hand-Stroking Elder. His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness takes her and changes her into a multitudinous and close-toothed comb, which he sticks into his august hair-bunch.

l: eight-forked serpent of Koshi, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: It has eight heads and eight tails, eyes like akakagachi, and a body covered with moss, chamaecyparis, and cryptomerias. Its length extends over eight valleys and eight hills, and its belly is constantly bloody and inflamed. It drinks from eight vats of liquor, becomes intoxicated and sleeps, and is then cut into pieces by His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness.

l: eight-fold refined liquor, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: It is prepared in eight vats as part of the trap for the eight-forked serpent of Koshi. The serpent drinks it and becomes intoxicated.

l: ten-grasp sabre, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness draws the ten-grasp sabre that is girded on him and uses it to cut the eight-forked serpent into pieces.

l: Herb-Quelling Great Sword, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: A great sword is found inside the middle tail of the eight-forked serpent after the edge of the ten-grasp sabre breaks. His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness takes it and reports it to the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity; it is called the Herb-Quelling Great Sword.

l: descent from Heaven, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness descends from Heaven to Tori-kami at the head-waters of the River Hi. He identifies himself as elder brother to the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity.

l: annual devouring of the daughters, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The eight-forked serpent of Koshi has come every year and devoured one of Foot-Stroking-Elder and Hand-Stroking Elder's eight daughters. Wondrous-Inada-Princess is the remaining daughter awaiting its next arrival.

l: preparation of the liquor trap, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness orders Foot-Stroking-Elder and Hand-Stroking Elder to prepare eight-fold refined liquor, build a fence with eight gates, tie eight platforms to the gates, and place a liquor-vat on each platform. The preparations are completed as instructed.

l: serpent's intoxication, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The eight-forked serpent dips one head into each vat and drinks the liquor. It becomes intoxicated, and all its heads lie down and sleep.

l: slaying of the eight-forked serpent, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness draws his ten-grasp sabre and cuts the sleeping eight-forked serpent into pieces. The River Hi consequently flows as a river of blood.

l: discovery of the great sword, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: When the edge of the ten-grasp sabre breaks while cutting the serpent's middle tail, His-Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness investigates and finds a great sword inside. He takes it and respectfully informs the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: His Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness searched in Idzumo for a place to build a palace and arrived at Suga. He said his august heart was pure there and built the palace of Suga. When the palace was first built, clouds rose, and he made an august song about eight clouds and the eight-fold fence of Idzumo. He appointed Deity Foot-Stroking-Elder as Headman of the palace and bestowed on him the name Master-of-the-Temple-of-Inada-Eight-Eared-Deity-of-Suga.

l: Crying and Weeping of His Impetuous-Male-Augustness, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: His Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness searched in Idzumo for a place to build a palace, arrived at Suga, and built the palace of Suga there. He made an august song when clouds rose from the newly built palace. He appointed Deity Foot-Stroking-Elder as Headman of the palace and bestowed on him the name Master-of-the-Temple-of-Inada-Eight-Eared-Deity-of-Suga.

l: Land of Idzumo, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Idzumo was the land where His Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness searched for a place to build a palace. The august song says that the eight-fold fence of Idzumo makes an eight-fold fence for the spouses to retire within.

l: Suga, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Suga was the place where His Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness built a palace after saying that his august heart was pure there. The place is now called Suga, and clouds rose from it when the palace was first built.

l: palace of Suga, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The palace of Suga was built by His Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness at Suga for him to dwell in. Clouds rose from it when it was first built, and Deity Foot-Stroking-Elder was appointed its Headman.

l: august song, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The august song was made by His Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness when clouds rose from the palace of Suga. It said that eight clouds arise and that the eight-fold fence of Idzumo makes an eight-fold fence for the spouses to retire within.

l: eight-fold fence of Idzumo, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The eight-fold fence of Idzumo is described in the august song as making an eight-fold fence for the spouses to retire within.

l: old man (Foot-Stroking-Elder), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Deity Foot-Stroking-Elder was appointed by His Swift-Impetuous-Male-Augustness as Headman of the palace. He was also given the name Master-of-the-Temple-of-Inada-Eight-Eared-Deity-of-Suga.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The unit recounts the ancestry of the Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land. It traces a succession of marriages and births from the Deity Eight-Island Ruler through several generations. The Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land is identified by four other names, making five names in all.

l: The August Ancestors of the Deity-Master-of-the-Great Land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The August Ancestors of the Deity-Master-of-the-Great Land are presented through a genealogy of marriages and births. The lineage culminates in the Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land.

l: Deity Eight-Island Ruler, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Deity Eight-Island Ruler was begotten by the procreation of the unnamed parents in the thalamo. He wedded Princess-Falling-Like-the-Flowers-of-the-Trees, daughter of the Deity Great-Mountain-Possessor, and begot the Deity Fuha-no-moji-Ku-nu-su-nu.

l: Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land was begotten by the Deity Heavenly-Brandishing-Prince-Lord and the Young-Princess-of-the-Small-Country. He is also called the Deity Great-Name-Possessor, the Deity-of-the-Reed-Plains, the Deity of Eight-Thousand-Spears, and the Deity-Spirit-of-the-Living-Land.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land’s eighty brethren travel to Inaba seeking to marry the Princess of Yakami, taking him along as an attendant. At Cape Keta, the eighty Deities deceive the White Hare of Inaba, but the Deity Great-Name-Possessor heals it after hearing its story. The hare foretells that the Princess of Yakami will marry the Deity Great-Name-Possessor. The eighty Deities then repeatedly attempt to kill him, but his august parent restores him and sends him to the Deity Great-House-Prince in Ki.

l: Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land is taken to Inaba by his eighty brethren as an attendant carrying their bag. The White Hare of Inaba later foretells that he will obtain the Princess of Yakami.

l: eighty Deities, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The eighty Deities travel to Inaba because each wishes to marry the Princess of Yakami. They deceive and injure the White Hare of Inaba, and later repeatedly attempt to kill the Deity Great-Name-Possessor, but he is restored and escapes them.

l: Princess of Yakami, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Princess of Yakami refuses the proposals of the eighty Deities and declares that she will marry the Deity Great-Name-Possessor.

l: White Hare of Inaba, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The White Hare of Inaba tries to cross from the Island of Oki by deceiving the crocodiles, but the last crocodile strips off its clothing. After following the eighty Deities’ harmful instructions, it is healed by the Deity Great-Name-Possessor and becomes known as the Hare Deity.

l: Inaba, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Inaba is the land associated with the Princess of Yakami and the White Hare of Inaba. The eighty Deities travel there seeking the princess, and Cape Keta is where they encounter the hare.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Deity Great-Name-Possessor goes to the Nether-Distant-Land, where His Impetuous-Male-Augustness tests him with snakes, centipedes, wasps, and fire. With help from the Forward-Princess and a mouse, he survives, escapes after tying up the Great Deity, and takes the great life-sword, life-bow-and-arrows, and heavenly speaking-lute. At the Even Pass of Hades, the Great Deity commands him to pursue his half-brethren and become Master-of-the-Great-Land and Spirit-of-the-Living-Land. The Deity Great-Name-Possessor scatters the eighty Deities and begins to make the land, while the Forward-Princess bears a child called the Tree-Fork-Deity and the Deity-of-August-Wells.

l: Nether-Distant-Land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Nether-Distant-Land is where His Impetuous-Male-Augustness dwells. The Deity Great-Name-Possessor goes there to receive his counsel.

l: Crying and Weeping of His Impetuous-Male-Augustness, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: His Impetuous-Male-Augustness receives the Deity Great-Name-Possessor and tests him by sending him into a snake-house, a centipede and wasp-house, and a burning moor. He later pursues him to the Even Pass of Hades and commands him to pursue his half-brethren and become Master-of-the-Great-Land and Spirit-of-the-Living-Land.

l: Forward-Princess, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Forward-Princess sees the Deity Great-Name-Possessor, marries him, and gives him scarves that protect him from snakes, centipedes, and wasps. She helps him escape and later bears a child called the Tree-Fork-Deity and the Deity-of-August-Wells.

l: Deity Great-Name-Possessor, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Deity Great-Name-Possessor survives the trials imposed by His Impetuous-Male-Augustness with help from the Forward-Princess and a mouse. He ties up the Great Deity, escapes with the great life-sword, life-bow-and-arrows, and heavenly speaking-lute, pursues the eighty Deities, and begins to make the land.

l: great life-sword, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The great life-sword is taken by the Deity Great-Name-Possessor when he escapes from the Great Deity. At the Even Pass of Hades, the Great Deity tells him to use it to pursue his half-brethren.

l: life-bow-and-arrows, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The life-bow-and-arrows are taken by the Deity Great-Name-Possessor when he escapes from the Great Deity. The Great Deity tells him to use them to pursue his half-brethren.

l: Even Pass of Hades, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Even Pass of Hades is where the Great Deity pursues the Deity Great-Name-Possessor and calls out commands to him from afar.

l: half-brethren, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The half-brethren are to be pursued by the Deity Great-Name-Possessor with the great life-sword and life-bow-and-arrows until they crouch on the august slopes of the passes and are swept into the reaches of the rivers.

l: eighty Deities, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The eighty Deities are pursued and scattered by the Deity Great-Name-Possessor. He pursues them until they crouch on the august slope of every pass and are swept into every river.

l: Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Master-of-the-Great-Land is a role the Great Deity commands the Deity Great-Name-Possessor to assume after pursuing his half-brethren.

l: Spirit-of-the-Living-Land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Spirit-of-the-Living-Land is another role the Great Deity commands the Deity Great-Name-Possessor to assume, with the Forward-Princess as his consort.

l: Mount Uka, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Mount Uka is named as the place at whose foot the Deity Great-Name-Possessor is commanded to make stout the temple-pillars in the nethermost rock-bottom.

l: land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Deity Great-Name-Possessor is commanded to become Master-of-the-Great-Land and begins to make the land after pursuing and scattering the eighty Deities.

l: land-making, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Land-making begins after the Deity Great-Name-Possessor pursues and scatters the eighty Deities. He is commanded to make the land as Master-of-the-Great-Land and Spirit-of-the-Living-Land.

l: marriage, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Forward-Princess and the Deity Great-Name-Possessor exchange glances and are married. The Great Deity later commands that she become his consort.

l: escape from the Great Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Deity Great-Name-Possessor escapes from the Great Deity after tying his hair to the rafters and blocking the floor with a five hundred draught rock. He carries off the great life-sword, life-bow-and-arrows, and heavenly speaking-lute, though the lute's sound causes the Great Deity to pull down the house.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Deity-of-Eight-Thousand-Spears travels to the Land of Koshi to woo the Princess of Nuna-kaha, having heard that she is wise and beautiful. He sings outside her house, lamenting that the birds and cock interrupt his wooing. The Princess of Nuna-kaha answers from inside with songs expressing maidenly reserve and promising to come forth at night. They do not cohabit that night, but they cohabit augustly on the following night.

l: Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: He goes to the Land of Koshi to woo the Princess of Nuna-kaha after failing to find a spouse in the Land of the Eight islands. He sings outside her house and later cohabits augustly with her on the following night.

l: Princess of Nuna-kaha, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: She is described as a wise and beautiful maiden in the Land of Koshi. She answers the Deity-of-Eight-Thousand-Spears from inside her house in songs, saying she will come forth at night, and cohabits augustly with him on the following night.

l: Land of Koshi, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Land of Koshi is the distant land where the Princess of Nuna-kaha lives. The Deity-of-Eight-Thousand-Spears travels there to woo her.

l: wooing of the Deity-of-Eight-Thousand-Spears, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The wooing takes place at the house of the Princess of Nuna-kaha. The Deity-of-Eight-Thousand-Spears sings outside while the Princess responds from inside, and the wooing culminates in their coition on the following night.

l: coition of the Deity-of-Eight-Thousand-Spears and the Princess of Nuna-kaha, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Deity-of-Eight-Thousand-Spears and the Princess of Nuna-kaha do not cohabit on the night of his arrival and their songs. They cohabit augustly on the following night.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The unit concerns the Deity-of-Eight-Thousand-Spears and Her Augustness the Forward-Princess. Because the Deity's Chief Empress is very jealous, the Deity prepares to depart from Idzumo for the Land of Yamato. Her Augustness the Forward-Princess offers him an august liquor-cup and sings of her exclusive bond with him. They pledge each other by the cup with their hands on each other's necks, and this is called the Cup Pledge and is said to continue to the present time.

l: Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Deity-of-Eight-Thousand-Spears prepares to leave Idzumo for the Land of Yamato because his Chief Empress is jealous. He sings about his departure and pledges himself by the cup with Her Augustness the Forward-Princess.

l: Her Augustness the Forward-Princess, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Her Augustness the Forward-Princess is the Deity's Chief Empress and is very jealous. She offers him an august liquor-cup, sings that she has no man or spouse except him, and pledges herself to him.

l: Land of Idzumo, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Idzumo is the place from which the Deity is about to depart.

l: the Land of Yamato, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Land of Yamato is the place to which the Deity is about to go from Idzumo.

l: the Deity's departure from Idzumo to the Land of Yamato, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Deity's departure from Idzumo to the Land of Yamato is prompted by distress over his Chief Empress's jealousy. He sings about flocking and departing before the cup pledge takes place.

l: the Cup Pledge, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Cup Pledge occurs when the Deity and Her Augustness the Forward-Princess pledge each other by the cup with their hands on each other's necks. They are said to remain at rest until the present time, and the pledge is called divine words.

l: august liquor-cup, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The august liquor-cup is taken and offered by Her Augustness the Forward-Princess to the Deity. It is used for their pledge.

l: the Deity's jealousy, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Deity's jealousy is not described; the text says that the Deity's Chief Empress, Her Augustness the Forward-Princess, is very jealous.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The unit concerns the descendants of the Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land. He fathers several children through marriages with various deities and princesses, beginning with Deity Aji-shiki-taka-hiko-ne and continuing through Deity Toho-tsu-yama-zaki-tarashi. The text identifies Deity Aji-shiki-taka-hiko-ne as the Great August Deity of Kamo. From the Deity Eight-Island-Ruler through Deity Toho-tsu-yama-zaki-tarashi, the descendants are called the Deities of seventeen generations.

l: Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land wedded several deities and princesses and begot children, beginning with Deity Aji-shiki-taka-hiko-ne and continuing through Deity Toho-tsu-yama-zaki-tarashi.

l: Deity Aji-shiki-taka-hiko-ne, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Deity Aji-shiki-taka-hiko-ne was begotten by the Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land and Her Augustness Torrent-Mist-Princess. He is now called the Great August Deity of Kamo.

l: Deity Bird-Growing-Ears, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Deity Bird-Growing-Ears was begotten by the Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land and the Deity Bird-Ears. This Deity wedded Hina-teri-nakata-bichi-wo-ikochini and begot Deity Land-Great-Wealth.

l: Deity Land-Great-Wealth, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Deity Land-Great-Wealth was begotten by Deity Bird-Growing-Ears and Hina-teri-nakata-bichi-wo-ikochini. This Deity wedded the Deity Ashi-nadaka and begot Deity Swift-Awful-Brave-Sahaya-Land-Ruler.

l: Deity Swift-Awful-Brave-Sahaya-Land-Ruler, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Deity Swift-Awful-Brave-Sahaya-Land-Ruler was begotten by Deity Land-Great-Wealth and the Deity Ashi-nadaka. This Deity wedded Princess Luck-Spirit and begot Deity Awful-Master-Prince.

l: Deity Awful-Master-Prince, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Deity Awful-Master-Prince was begotten by Deity Swift-Awful-Brave-Sahaya-Land-Ruler and Princess Luck-Spirit. This Deity wedded Princess Hina-rashi and begot Deity Tahiri-kishi-marumi.

l: Deity Tahiri-kishi-marumi, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Deity Tahiri-kishi-marumi was begotten by Deity Awful-Master-Prince and Princess Hina-rashi. This Deity wedded the Deity Princess-Life-Spirit-Luck-Spirit and begot Deity Mira-na-mi.

l: Deity Mira-na-mi, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Deity Mira-na-mi was begotten by Deity Tahiri-kishi-marumi and the Deity Princess-Life-Spirit-Luck-Spirit. This Deity wedded Princess Awo-numa-oshi and begot Deity Nunoshi-tomi-tori-naru-mi.

l: Deity Nunoshi-tomi-tori-naru-mi, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Deity Nunoshi-tomi-tori-naru-mi was begotten by Deity Mira-na-mi and Princess Awo-numa-oshi. This Deity wedded the Young-Day-Female-Deity and begot Deity Heavenly-Hibara-Great-Long-Wind-Wealth.

l: Deity Heavenly-Hibara-Great-Long-Wind-Wealth, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Deity Heavenly-Hibara-Great-Long-Wind-Wealth was begotten by Deity Nunoshi-tomi-tori-naru-mi and the Young-Day-Female-Deity. This Deity wedded the Deity Toho-tsu-ma-chi-ne and begot Deity Toho-tsu-yama-zaki-tarashi.

l: Deity Toho-tsu-yama-zaki-tarashi, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Deity Toho-tsu-yama-zaki-tarashi was begotten by Deity Heavenly-Hibara-Great-Long-Wind-Wealth and the Deity Toho-tsu-ma-chi-ne. The text places this Deity at the end of the line called the Deities of seventeen generations.

l: Deity Eight-Island Ruler, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The text states that from the Deity Eight-Island-Ruler down to Deity Toho-tsu-yama-zaki-tarashi are called the Deities of seventeen generations.

l: Deities of seventeen generations, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Deities of seventeen generations are identified as extending from the Deity Eight-Island-Ruler down to Deity Toho-tsu-yama-zaki-tarashi.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land dwelt at the august cape of Miho in Idzumo when the Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity arrived in a boat of heavenly Kagami dressed in skins of geese. The Crumbling Prince identified him as the child of the Deity-Producing-Wondrous-Deity, who declared that the two should become brethren and make and consolidate the land. The Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity and the Great-Name-Possessor then made and consolidated the land conjointly until the Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity crossed over to the Eternal Land.

l: Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land dwelt at the august cape of Miho in Idzumo. He encountered the Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity and sought to learn his name.

l: Land of Idzumo, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Idzumo was where the Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land dwelt at the august cape of Miho.

l: the Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity arrived riding on the crest of the waves in a boat of heavenly Kagami and dressed in skins of geese. He was identified as the child of the Deity-Producing-Wondrous-Deity, made and consolidated the land conjointly with the Great-Name-Possessor, and later crossed over to the Eternal Land.

l: the Crumbling Prince, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Crumbling Prince identified the unnamed Deity as the Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity. He is what is now called the scarecrow in the mountain fields, and he is a Deity who knows everything in the Empire though his legs do not walk.

l: the Deity-Producing-Wondrous-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Deity-Producing-Wondrous-Deity was identified as the parent of the Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity. He declared that the Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity and the Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land should become brethren and make and consolidate the land.

l: the land of Idzumo, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The land was made and consolidated conjointly by the Great-Name-Possessor and the Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity.

l: the two Deities the Great-Name-Possessor and the Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The two Deities the Great-Name-Possessor and the Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity made and consolidated the land conjointly. Their work continued until the Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity crossed over to the Eternal Land.

l: making and consolidating the land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Making and consolidating the land was the joint work of the Great-Name-Possessor and the Little-Prince-the-Renowned-Deity, after they were instructed to become brethren.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land laments that he cannot make the land alone and asks with what Deity he can make it. Deity illuminating the sea says the land can be made together if that Deity is laid to rest well. Deity illuminating the sea requests reverent worship on Yamato's green fence, the eastern mountain's top, and is identified as the Deity who dwells on the top of Mount Mimoro.

l: Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land laments that he cannot make the land alone and asks with what Deity he can make it. He asks how Deity illuminating the sea should be reverently laid to rest.

l: land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The land cannot be made by Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land alone. Deity illuminating the sea says the land can be made together with Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land if Deity illuminating the sea is laid to rest well.

l: Deity illuminating the sea, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Deity illuminating the sea appears and offers to make the land together with Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land if reverently laid to rest. Deity illuminating the sea requests reverent worship on Yamato's green fence, the eastern mountain's top, and dwells on the top of Mount Mimoro.

l: Yamato's green fence, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Yamato's green fence is named as the place where Deity illuminating the sea should be reverently worshipped.

l: eastern mountain's top, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The eastern mountain's top is named as the place where Deity illuminating the sea should be reverently worshipped.

l: Mount Mimoro, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Mount Mimoro is identified as the mountain whose top is the dwelling place of Deity illuminating the sea.

l: making the land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Making the land is an undertaking that Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land cannot accomplish alone. Deity illuminating the sea offers to undertake making the land together with Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land.

l: reverently worshipping the Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Reverently worshipping the Deity is required at Yamato's green fence, the eastern mountain's top, in order for Deity illuminating the sea to be laid to rest well.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Great-Harvest-Deity weds three princesses and fathers sixteen deities, including the Swift-Mountain-Dwelling Deity. The text lists the names and alternate names of these children and identifies several of their dwelling places and functions. The Swift-Mountain-Dwelling Deity weds the Deity Princess-of-Great-Food and fathers eight deities.

l: Great-Harvest-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Great-Harvest-Deity weds the Princess [of?] Inu, the Refulgent-Princess, and Princess Ame-shiru-karu-midzu. He fathers sixteen deities, from the Deity August-Spirit-of-the-Great-Land to the Great-Earth-Deity.

l: Swift-Mountain-Dwelling, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Swift-Mountain-Dwelling Deity weds the Deity Princess-of-Great-Food and fathers eight deities, from the Deity Young-Mountain-Integrator to the Deity Lord-Stem-Tree-Young-House-Rope.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity commands that the Luxuriant-Reed-Plains-the-Land-of-Fresh-Rice-ears-of-a-Thousand-Autumns,, Of Long-Five-Hundred-Autumns be governed by Truly-Conqueror-I-Conquer-Conquering-Swift-Heavenly-Great-Great-Ears. After observing that the land is painfully uproarious, Truly-Conqueror-I-Conquer-Conquering-Swift-Heavenly-Great-Great-Ears reports back to the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity. The High-August-Producing-Wondrous-Deity and the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity convene the eight hundred myriad Deities and ask Deity Thought-Includer to devise a plan for subduing the violent and savage Earthly Deities. They choose Deity Ame-no-ho-hi, but he curries favour with Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land and sends no report for three years.

l: The August Deliberation for Pacifying the Land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The August Deliberation for Pacifying the Land concerns the divine consultation over how to subdue the violent and savage Earthly Deities and establish governance of the land.

l: Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity commands that the land be governed by Truly-Conqueror-I-Conquer-Conquering-Swift-Heavenly-Great-Great-Ears. She later joins the High-August-Producing-Wondrous-Deity in convening the eight hundred myriad Deities and sending Deity Ame-no-ho-hi.

l: Central Land of Reed-Plains, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Luxuriant-Reed-Plains-the-Land-of-Fresh-Rice-ears-of-a-Thousand-Autumns,, Of Long-Five-Hundred-Autumns is the land assigned to Truly-Conqueror-I-Conquer-Conquering-Swift-Heavenly-Great-Great-Ears to govern. It is described as painfully uproarious and as containing numerous violent and savage Earthly Deities.
