l: Truly-Conqueror-I-Conquer-Conquering-Swift-Heavenly-Great-Great-Ears, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Truly-Conqueror-I-Conquer-Conquering-Swift-Heavenly-Great-Great-Ears is commanded to govern the land. After standing on the Floating Bridge of Heaven and observing that the land is painfully uproarious, he re-ascends and informs the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity.

l: eight hundred myriad Deities, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The eight hundred myriad Deities are assembled in a divine assembly in the bed of the Tranquil River of Heaven. They take counsel with Deity Thought-Includer and agree that Deity Ame-no-ho-hi should be sent to subdue the violent and savage Earthly Deities.

l: Deity Thought-Includer, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Deity Thought-Includer is caused to think of a plan concerning how to subdue the violent and savage Earthly Deities. He and the eight hundred myriad Deities decide that Deity Ame-no-ho-hi should be sent.

l: Earthly Deities, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Earthly Deities are numerous in the land and are described as violent and savage. The divine assembly seeks to send a deity to subdue them.

l: Deity Ame-no-ho-hi, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Deity Ame-no-ho-hi is selected and sent to subdue the Earthly Deities. He immediately curries favour with Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land and brings back no report for three years.

l: Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land receives Deity Ame-no-ho-hi, who curries favour with him after being sent to subdue the Earthly Deities.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The High-August-Producing-Wondrous-Deity and the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity send the Heavenly-Young-Prince to the Central Land of Reed-Plains after Deity Ame-no-ho-hi fails to return a report. The Heavenly-Young-Prince marries Princess Under-Shining, delays reporting for eight years, and is killed by an arrow after shooting the pheasant the Name-Crying-Female. His family builds a mourning-house, and the Deity Ajishiki-taka-hiko-ne destroys it after being mistaken for the dead prince. His younger sister sings a Song to reveal his august name.

l: Heavenly-Young-Prince, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Heavenly-Young-Prince is sent to the Central Land of Reed-Plains with heavenly feathered arrows to subdue and pacify its savage Deities. He marries Princess Under-Shining, brings back no report for eight years, shoots the pheasant the Name-Crying-Female, and dies when the returning arrow strikes him while he sleeps.

l: High-August-Producing-Wondrous-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The High-August-Producing-Wondrous-Deity asks which Deity should be sent to investigate the Heavenly-Young-Prince's failure to report. It is also another name for the High-Integrating-Deity.

l: Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity joins the High-August-Producing-Wondrous-Deity in asking which Deity should be sent after the Heavenly-Young-Prince fails to report.

l: Deity Ame-no-ho-hi, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Deity Ame-no-ho-hi is sent to the Central Land of Reed-Plains but is long of bringing back a report.

l: Central Land of Reed-Plains, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Central Land of Reed-Plains is the land to which the Heavenly-Young-Prince is sent to subdue and pacify its savage Deities.

l: Deity Thought-Includer, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Deity Thought-Includer recommends that the Heavenly-Young-Prince be sent. Later, Deity Thought-Includer joins the other Deities in recommending the pheasant the Name-Crying-Female as a messenger.

l: Deity Heaven's-Earth-Spirit, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Deity Heaven's-Earth-Spirit is the father of the Heavenly-Young-Prince. He comes down from Heaven with his wife and children after hearing the prince's wife's wailing and takes part in the mourning rites.

l: Her Augustness Princess Under-Shining, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Princess Under-Shining is the daughter of the Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land and marries the Heavenly-Young-Prince. Her wailing after his death reaches Heaven.

l: pheasant the Name-Crying-Female, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The pheasant the Name-Crying-Female is sent to ask the Heavenly-Young-Prince why he has brought back no report. It is shot and killed by him after the Heavenly-Spying-Woman calls its cry bad, and it does not return.

l: arrow, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The arrow bestowed on the Heavenly-Young-Prince is used to kill the pheasant the Name-Crying-Female. After the High-Integrating-Deity sends it back down through the arrow's hole, it strikes and kills the Heavenly-Young-Prince.

l: High-Integrating-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The High-Integrating-Deity finds blood on the arrow that reaches the august place where it is sitting with the Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity. It sends the arrow back down so that it kills the Heavenly-Young-Prince, and the text identifies it as another name for the High-August-Producing-Wondrous-Deity.

l: mourning-house, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: A mourning-house is built for the Heavenly-Young-Prince by his father, wife, and children after they come down from Heaven. The Deity Ajishiki-taka-hiko-ne cuts it down and kicks away its pieces after being mistaken for the dead prince.

l: Deity Aji-shiki-taka-hiko-ne, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Deity Ajishiki-taka-hiko-ne comes to condole on the mourning for the Heavenly-Young-Prince. Angered when mistaken for the dead prince, it cuts down and kicks away the mourning-house, then flies away.

l: Great-Blade-Mower, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Great-Blade-Mower is one name of the great sword used by the Deity Ajishiki-taka-hiko-ne to cut down the mourning-house.

l: Divine-Keen-Sabre, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Divine-Keen-Sabre is another name for the great sword used by the Deity Ajishiki-taka-hiko-ne to cut down the mourning-house.

l: Song, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: The Song is sung by the younger sister of the Deity Ajishiki-taka-hiko-ne to reveal his august name. It describes the Deity Aji-shiki-Taka-Hiko-Ne traversing two august valleys and is identified as being of a Rustic Style.

l: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity and the other Deities sent Brave-Awful-Possessing-Male-Deity and Deity Heavenly-Bird-Boat to ask Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land to yield the Central Land of Reed-Plains to the august child of the Heavenly Deities. Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land's sons, Deity Eight-Fold-Thing-Sign-Master and Deity Brave-August-Name-Firm, agreed to follow the command after Deity Brave-August-Name-Firm lost a trial of strength. Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land then agreed to yield up the Central Land of Reed-Plains if a great abode were established for him and his children were respectfully served. Brave-Awful-Possessing-Male-Deity re-ascended to Heaven and reported that he had subdued and pacified the Central Land of Reed-Plains.

l: Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Heaven-Shining-Great-August-Deity asked which Deity should be sent on a fresh mission and charged Brave-Awful-Possessing-Male-Deity and Deity Heavenly-Bird-Boat to ask Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land about yielding the Central Land of Reed-Plains.

l: Brave-Awful-Possessing-Male-Deity, Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters), Volume I (The Age of the Gods), Sect.
s: Brave-Awful-Possessing-Male-Deity was offered by his father, Deity Heaven-Point-Blade-Extended, and sent with Deity Heavenly-Bird-Boat to obtain the Central Land of Reed-Plains. He defeated Deity Brave-August-Name-Firm in a trial of strength, secured Deity Master-of-the-Great-Land's agreement to yield the land, and reported to Heaven that he had subdued and pacified it.
